summary.name: Shotcut
summary.one_liner: Shotcut is a free, open source, cross-platform video editor for Windows, Mac and Linux built on the MLT framework and FFmpeg.
use_cases: Editing video on Windows, Mac or Linux
Editing mixed-format video without converting first
Capturing video from SDI or HDMI devices
summary.what_it_does: Shotcut is a video editor that supports hundreds of audio and video formats and codecs through FFmpeg, and it can edit native files without an import step. Projects can mix formats, resolutions and frame rates on one timeline, and it supports resolutions up to 4K. It can capture from Blackmagic Design SDI and HDMI devices, webcams, screen (X11), JACK and Pulse audio, IP streams and Windows DirectShow devices. The interface has dockable and undockable panels, and keyboard shortcuts for J/K/L playback, I/O in-out points and frame or second stepping. The page says versions are date-based and new releases come about every two months, and that multiple versions can be kept installed.
notable: Native editing of many formats via FFmpeg with no import step
Capture from Blackmagic SDI/HDMI, webcam, screen and IP streams
Date-based versioning with new releases about every two months, multiple versions can be kept
Originally conceived in 2004 by Charlie Yates; current version is a rewrite by Dan Dennedy
caveats: Page does not describe paid tiers; listing marks it as freeware and open source
Some capture sources (DirectShow, JACK, Pulse, X11) are platform-specific
